records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the above location for accident involving a pedestrian in a private lot. upon arrival i observed unit 2 laying on the ground directly in front of unit 1. i approached unit 2 who was being attended by ems. i observed that the location of where the accident happened was well lit and had heavy foot traffic. i immediately started to clear out bystanders and identify witnesses of the accident. i spoke to two witnesses individually who had similar narratives to the accident. all stated that unit 1 was driving south in the private lot and was making a left turn in the parking lot and that unit 2 was walking through the private lot at the time that unit 1 was making the left turn. both witnesses i talked to stated that unit 1 was not driving at a high rate of speed. both witnesses stated that unit 1 struck unit 2 and stopped on top of unit 2. both stated that unit 1 reversed off unit 2 and the two occupants of unit 1 got out of the vehicle. i spoke to the passenger of unit 1 who stated that the driver of unit 1 had drank 4-6 beers at the location. the location of the crash had cameras that pointed in the direction of the accident. employees at the location provided video of the accident and the video coincided with the narrative that the two witnesses had given to me. this crash report was supplemented on [date] by tid det. b. martinez #2477 to update details due to the victim's death and to add the results of the toxicology report, which indicated unit 1 driver's bac was 0. 156 (+/- 0. 009) grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood.

records.public_safe_text: police responded to the above location for accident involving a pedestrian in a private lot. upon arrival i observed unit 2 laying on the ground directly in front of unit 1. i approached unit 2 who was being attended by ems. i observed that the location of where the accident happened was well lit and had heavy foot traffic. i immediately started to clear out bystanders and identify witnesses of the accident. i spoke to two witnesses individually who had similar narratives to the accident. all stated that unit 1 was driving south in the private lot and was making a left turn in the parking lot and that unit 2 was walking through the private lot at the time that unit 1 was making the left turn. both witnesses i talked to stated that unit 1 was not driving at a high rate of speed. both witnesses stated that unit 1 struck unit 2 and stopped on top of unit 2. both stated that unit 1 reversed off unit 2 and the two occupants of unit 1 got out of the vehicle. i spoke to the passenger of unit 1 who stated that the driver of unit 1 had drank 4-6 beers at the location. the location of the crash had cameras that pointed in the direction of the accident. employees at the location provided video of the accident and the video coincided with the narrative that the two witnesses had given to me. this crash report was supplemented on [date] by tid det. b. martinez #2477 to update details due to the victim's death and to add the results of the toxicology report, which indicated unit 1 driver's bac was 0. 156 (+/- 0. 009) grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood.

left-turn (northbound direction) in the lot to pull next to a fuel pump. unit-1 stated as she began to make her turn she heard her daughter (devin scherman, the front passenger) suddenly shout, ""you're going to hit her!"" suddenly unit-1 saw a female adult (unit-2) hit against her front-left quarter panel, causing unit-2 to be knocked down backwards and fall to the ground. unit-1 exited her vehicle and immediately went to check on unit-2, who was stating that she had hit her head on the ground. unit-1 assisted unit-2 in standing up and getting her inside the convenience store, where she immediately contacted emergency personnel. no damage was caused to unit-1's vehicle, nor did i observe any damage as a result of the collision. paramedics with the frisco fire department were in the rear office of the convenience store assessing the patient, where i was informed she had a bump (swelling) on the back of her head and a small abrasion on her right thumb. unit-2 informed paramedics records.public_safe_text: on wednesday, [date], i, officer n. oliva #3666, working as patrol unit #153, was dispatched to the ""walmart fuel station,"" located at 335 [roadway] in frisco, denton county, texas, regarding a motor vehicle collision involving a pedestrian (cfs [identifier]). upon my arrival, i contacted dana scherman (unit-1), who was the driver of her vehicle (a silver 2011 jeep wrangler), and asked her what happened. unit-1 stated she was driving through the ""walmart fuel station"" lot, in between the fuel pumps and the convenience store, and was starting to make a left-turn (northbound direction) in the lot to pull next to a fuel pump. unit-1 stated as she began to make her turn she heard her daughter (devin scherman, the front passenger) suddenly shout, ""you're going to hit her!"" suddenly unit-1 saw a female adult (unit-2) hit against her front-left quarter panel, causing unit-2 to be knocked down backwards and fall to the ground. unit-1 exited her vehicle and immediately went to check on unit-2, who was stating that she had hit her head on the ground. unit-1 assisted unit-2 in standing up and getting her inside the convenience store, where she immediately contacted emergency personnel. no damage was caused to unit-1's vehicle, nor did i observe any damage as a result of the collision. paramedics with the frisco fire department were in the rear office of the convenience store assessing the patient, where i was informed she had a bump (swelling) on the back of her head and a small abrasion on her right thumb. unit-2 informed paramedics that she did not wish to be medically transported and would go at a later time with her husband if needed. unit-2 stated she had exited from her vehicle, which was parked beside fuel pump #15, along the northeast corner of the fuel stations, and was walking into the convenience store to pay for her fuel. unit-2 stated as she began to cross the parking lot located between the fuel pumps and convenience store, a silver-coloured jeep (unit-1), which was travelling straight through the lot (eastbound) suddenly made a sharp left-turn in front of her. unit-2 stated she was unable to avoid the vehicle and was hit by the vehicle's front-left quarter panel, causing her to be knocked backwards and fall to the ground. unit-2 stated she then hit the back of her head on the ground, where she felt a sharp, dull pain, but claimed to have not lost consciousness. based on the statements provided above, in addition to this collision occurring on private property, i formed the opinion both units share equal fault in this collision. unit-1 failed to yield to pedestrian traffic in the parking lot of the fuel station lot, and unit-2 failed to yield to oncoming traffic in the parking lot.
